_comment: The version policy's verdict oracle (docs/VERSION_POLICY.md). One file, two
readers: conformance/test_version_policy.py runs every row through the
Python check_contract_version and reference/cpp/tests runs every row it can
through the C++ one, so the two references are measured against this file
and never against each other.
A row is a consumer's declared ACCEPTANCE (one MAJOR.MINOR floor per major
it accepts) plus the version a document declares, and the verdict the policy
owes: accept, accept_warn (accepted, and the higher minor is reported),
refuse (a data error the reader raises), or call_error (a PROGRAMMING error
in the accepted set itself, refused at call time and not at read time).
declared_kind exists because one reader is typed and the other is not. The
C++ entry point takes a std::string, so a row whose declared value is a JSON
number, null or list cannot be handed to it at all: the distinction was made
by the loader before the reader was called. Those rows are Python-only and
say so in their own field rather than being quietly absent.
What this oracle does NOT cover (META-2): warning DELIVERY. It says a higher
minor is accepted and reported; whether that arrives through Python's
warnings channel, how it is deduplicated, and what a host that escalates
warnings to errors sees are all owned by the tests in
conformance/test_version_policy.py. It also says nothing about which set a
given consumer should declare, nor about the three-step bump procedure that
set is meant to make shippable.

cases.name: one major, minor equal to the floor
cases.why: the ordinary read

cases.name: one major, minor below the floor
cases.why: an older minor of an accepted major carries nothing new

cases.name: one major, minor above the floor
cases.why: additive by construction, so it is read as 1.0 with the rest ignored, and the event is reported

cases.name: one major, the document is a lower major
cases.why: an older major is a different document shape; half-parsing it is worse than refusing

cases.name: one major, the document is a higher major
cases.why: the consumer has no code path for major 2

cases.name: two majors, the older one at its floor
cases.why: a transition window is open and the old major is still read

cases.name: two majors, the older one above its floor
cases.why: the minor rule applies per major, not to the set

cases.name: two majors, the newer one below its floor
cases.why: each major carries its own floor, and 2.1 is under 2.3

cases.name: two majors, the newer one at its floor
cases.why: the floor itself is accepted, silently

cases.name: two majors, the newer one above its floor
cases.why: same verdict as the one-major case, on the second entry

cases.name: two majors, a third one nobody accepts
cases.why: the refusal names EVERY accepted major, so the producer sees the whole window

cases.name: two majors, a document below both
cases.why: a lower major is refused whatever the size of the set

cases.name: patch present, at the floor
cases.why: PATCH is parsed and discarded; the normalized version drops it

cases.name: patch present, above the floor
cases.why: a patch never changes a verdict, so this is the higher-minor case

cases.name: patch present in the accepted set itself
cases.why: emitters already declare 1.0.0; a consumer may spell its floor the same way

cases.name: patch present on a refused major
cases.why: the patch does not rescue a major the consumer does not accept

cases.name: malformed: a major alone
cases.why: a version without a minor is not a version

cases.name: malformed: a v prefix
cases.why: digits only, the same rule the sidecar schemas' pattern states

cases.name: malformed: four components
cases.why: MAJOR.MINOR or MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, and nothing longer

cases.name: malformed: a trailing newline
cases.why: surrounding whitespace is malformed, not a version (SPEC-2); the schemas' pattern admits none

cases.name: malformed: a leading space
cases.why: same rule at the other end of the string

cases.name: a bare JSON number
cases.why: JSON cannot tell 1.0 from 1, and 1.10 would already have become 1.1; only a quoted string is a version

cases.name: a bare JSON integer, the legacy pins spelling
cases.why: pins.json's deprecated integer is normalized to "1.0" by the consumer, before the policy is applied

cases.name: missing
cases.why: an absent version is refused, not defaulted

cases.name: a structured value where a version belongs
cases.why: the components are not for a reader to reassemble

cases.name: call error: two floors for one major
cases.why: the consumer declared two floors for major 1 and there is no verdict to give; a programming error, refused at call time

cases.name: call error: two floors for one major, one spelled with a patch
cases.why: PATCH is discarded, so these are the same floor twice and the duplicate is not hidden by the spelling

cases.name: call error: an empty accepted set
cases.why: a consumer that accepts nothing can read nothing; silently refusing every document would look like bad data

cases.name: call error: a malformed entry in the accepted set
cases.why: a typo in the consumer must not read as a bad document
